name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Auto-apply whitespace-only patches to third-party dependencies using Pret. It’s safe, reversible, and fixes formatting drift without touching logic—no risk of breaking behavior. The trade-off is manual review of edge cases where whitespace changes could affect tooling (like code formatters), but those are rare and detectable.

name: Gauge
text: Risk isn’t just edge cases—whitespace patches to third-party deps can break tooling that parses ASTs (e.g., linters, bundlers) if they rely on exact token positions. Better alternative: auto-apply only to files where the repo’s own CI enforces formatting (e.g., Prettier config), and gate it on a test that checks AST stability post-patch. Settle it by running the patch on a sample of dependencies and verifying no CI failures.

Do it: Auto-apply whitespace-only patches to third-party dependencies using Pret, but only for files covered by the repo’s Prettier config. This ensures formatting drift is fixed without touching logic, and the repo’s own CI already enforces consistent formatting—so tooling like linters and bundlers won’t break. The trade-off is we exclude files without Prettier enforcement, leaving some drift unaddressed, but that’s safer than risking AST-sensitive tooling failures.

name: Gauge
text: Whitespace patches still risk breaking AST-sensitive tooling even under Prettier—AST parsers like Babel or Esbuild don’t care about your repo’s formatting rules. Better alternative: auto-apply only to files where the third-party dependency explicitly declares formatting stability (e.g., a `.prettierignore` or `prettier:ignore` in their docs). Settle it by testing whether the dependency’s CI passes with whitespace changes—if it fails, reject the patch.
